item.title: Dolphins' rebuild is working despite 1-7 record, and proof is on field
item.description: MIAMI GARDENS ― The Miami Dolphins may be the most optimistic, positive, encouraged 1-7 team in pro sports history and I'm all for it. "Bright future," Dolphins veteran linebacker Jordyn Brooks said after a 19-9 loss to the Detroit Lions that put a wrap on the first half of the Dolphins' 18-week NFL schedule. The Dolphins take too many penalties (11 on Sunday), wear down in the second half of games (little depth) and do not score enough red zone touchdowns (none on Sunday). Yet, somehow, nobody is crying, nobody is complaining and nobody is throwing water coolers. I'm all for it. That's because wins and losses were never an important part of evaluating the Dolphins' 2026 season. It's all the other stuff. And so far, all the other stuff has been, well, encouraging. "Right now, I'm angry because I hate to lose," Miami coach Jeff Hafley said , when asked if he is more encouraged than discouraged by the first half of his first NFL season. But then Hafley gave the important part of the answer: "I'm encouraged with this team. I'm encouraged the way they work. I'm encouraged because we've challenged them to play the game a certain way. I'm encouraged because we've asked them to practice a certain way. I'm encouraged because, in my opinion, the Detroit Lions are probably the most physical team in the world. Because in my opinion, the Detroit Lions are probably the most physical team in the NFL. And that's the way they coach and that's the way we play. And I would say we went toe to toe with them." Miami Dolphins rebuild roster set up this 1-7 record If that was bullcrap, I would call it out. It's not. The Dolphins are reaching their 2026 goals as set by ― me. Play hard. Relentless effort. Positive attitude and culture. Player growth and development. It's happening, despite that entirely irrelevant 1-7 record. "Our young guys, man, our rookies, I think that they, they got a bright future, man," said Brooks, the veteran linebacker. "I think Sully (GM Jon-Eric Sullivan) did a great job. Bring these guys in, he brought the right guys in, and not just because they're out there making plays, but just the right guys, right people that you want in the locker room to go through something like this one in seven losing. Losing is not easy, but I think it reveals who you are in that moment." It is a bit discouraging in the first half of the Dolphins' season that quarterback Malik Willis has not yet shown he can definitely be counted on as the 2027 starter. But it cannot be ruled out, either. In this game, Willis was hampered by a tight hamstring. There was also a "miscommunication" with breakout rookie receiver Caleb Douglas which led to an interception. That was a key play because Miami trailed only 6-3 in the second half. item.title: #23 Men’s Soccer Blanks #25 UCLA 2-0 to Reach the Big Ten Semifinals
item.description: SEATTLE, Wash. — Joshua Jerome had been on the field for 83 seconds when he scored. Matty Lynch had been on for 145. That was all Rutgers needed. The third-seeded Scarlet Knights beat sixth-seeded UCLA 2-0 in the Big Ten Tournament quarterfinals on Sunday afternoon at Husky Soccer Stadium. Rafael Ponce de Leon made five saves for Rutgers’ sixth clean sheet of the season, and it was the program’s first Big Ten Tournament win since they lifted the trophy at Yurcak Field in 2022. Rutgers came west at 8-6-2, 6-3-1 in the Big Ten and No. 23 in the country, back in the conference tournament for the first time since 2023 after finishing third in the league. They closed the regular season with a 4-1 win at No. 8 Michigan State on Oct. 30, when Amer Lukovic scored twice and Ponce de Leon saved a penalty with four minutes left, and on Tuesday the Big Ten named Ponce de Leon its Goalkeeper of the Week. The Scarlet Knights had already beaten UCLA once, 3-1 at Yurcak in the Big Ten opener on Sept. 11, a night when the Bruins scored in the third minute and did not put another shot on target. Sunday’s win was Rutgers’ second over UCLA in 58 days. UCLA arrived 9-3-5 and 4-3-3 in the Big Ten, ranked No. 25, and nearly did not arrive at all. The Bruins started the final day of the regular season seventh on 12 points with six teams qualifying, then beat No. 6 Washington 1-0 on Wednesday when Diego Castano scored from beyond midfield, his team-leading eighth goal of the year, and got the rest of what they needed from Northwestern’s win over Wisconsin. Ryan Jorden’s side were also the defending champions. As a four seed a year ago, UCLA won 2-0 at No. 1 Maryland and beat Michigan 5-0 in the final, and in October 2025 they had beaten Rutgers 5-2 in Westwood. Castano and Jaime Amaro, the Spaniard who transferred in from Bryant and has six goals and five assists this fall, carry the attack. Castano started Sunday on the bench. Ponce de Leon did not have to make a save the last time these teams met. He made five on Sunday. item.description: UPDATE: J.J. McCarthy , head to the sideline with an injury. Officially, McCarthy has a hip injury and is questionable to return. McCarthy slammed his helmet down on the bench before heading into the blue medical evaluation tent. Jameis Winston replaced him. As the Giants deal with life without Jaxson Dart, they benched Winston for McCarthy heading into their pre-bye week game in Houston. The Giants shockingly won that game in overtime. item.title: ‘Worth half a goal’ – Fermin Lopez hails Lamine Yamal’s assist as Barcelona beat Atletico
item.description: Fermin Lopez hailed Lamine Yamal for his excellent pass that set up Barcelona’s winner in a 2-1 victory over Atletico Madrid on Sunday night in La Liga. Barcelona went behind in the match but hit back through Lopez. The Spain star then added a second, firing home after a brilliant pass by Yamal. Lopez says Yamal’s contribution was worth “half a goal” as he celebrated a huge win at the top of the table in Spain. “May the connection with Lamine continue, we know each other very well, the pass for the second goal is half a goal, I’m very happy for him too,” he told Movistar. Barcelona looked out of sorts at the start of the match, going behind to Guiliano Simeone’s early goal, and Lopez admitted it was a tough encounter. “It was a very difficult match, last year they beat us in the Cup and Champions League, we knew what they were going to propose to us, but we knew how to come back from the game,” he explained. “We weren’t sharp, but with the goal we freed ourselves, played our game and won.” Victory sees Barcelona move five points clear of Atletico in the table, with Simeone’s men dropping to third after their defeat.

item.description: The Los Angeles Rams have an injury concern with wide receiver Puka Nacua following the Week 9 win over the Washington Commanders on Sunday. Late in the fourth quarter on the Rams’ final offensive snap, Nacua suffered a knee injury after a carry on third down. Nacua took a hard shot to his knee and was clearly shaken up after the play. According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter and NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo , Nacua is set to undergo an MRI on Monday to determine the severity of the injury. One of the best Monday Night Football games of the entire NFL season will take place in Week 9 when the Buffalo Bills go on the road to take on the Minnesota Vikings. The Bills, of course, are led by Josh Allen and one of the NFL’s best offenses. The Buffalo defense could use some work and is still getting some key players back from injury, but having arguably the best quarterback in the NFL on the other side gives the defense a lot of margin for error. The Bills also come into this game at 6-1 and are the only remaining one-loss team in the AFC, so they control their own destiny for the No. 1 seed in the conference at this point. There is a big pack of teams with two losses behind them, so getting wins in these kinds of games is very important for their chase for home-field. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) On the other side, the Vikings’ offense has been under the microscope. Adding Kyler Murray was supposed to unlock a new level for Kevin O’Connell’s group, but that didn’t necessarily happen for the Vikings over the first eight weeks of the season. Now, Murray is dealing with a hamstring injury and Carson Wentz is set to get the start on Monday night. On the other side, the Vikings have arguably the best defense in the NFL so far this season with Brian Flores running the show. That unit has led Minnesota to a 6-1 record and the top spot in a loaded NFC North. Nobody has been able to solve the Flores puzzle yet this season. Even the Lions and their explosive offense, in the Vikings’ only loss of the season, couldn’t find consistent answers against the Vikings. Now, Flores and company get to test themselves against one of the league’s best offenses once again. Where can Allen and the Bills poke at the Vikings on defense, and how will Minnesota’s aggressive attack cause problems for them? Can Minnesota force Josh Allen into obvious passing situations? After an up-and-down 4th quarter, the Broncos, with the help of a timely strip-sack by Nik Bonitto, came away with the win and improved to 7-2 on the year. The offense played well at times, but left points on the field due to some sloppy play. Key defensive plays by Devon Key and Nik Bonitto were game-changers and a big reason why the Broncos won this game. So, with all that said, here are my winners and losers from the Denver Broncos’ 26-21 victory over the Carolina Panthers. WINNER – Nik Bonitto, clutch strip-sack The defense and pass rush were not great for most of the game, more on that later, but once again, the Broncos’ defense and their pass rush came up big when it mattered most. item.description: Why Arsenal’s Full-Backs Are Crucial To Arteta’s Tactical System – Opinion One of the most interesting aspects of Mikel Arteta’s Arsenal is the way his team uses its full-backs. Traditionally, full-backs were expected to provide width, overlap with wingers and deliver crosses into the penalty area. Under Arteta, however, their responsibilities have become far more complex. Rather than simply staying out wide, Arsenal’s full-backs frequently move into central areas of the pitch, helping the team dominate possession and control midfield. This tactical approach, commonly known as using inverted full-backs, has become an important part of Arsenal’s identity, as Dan Smith explored in Arteta’s tactical evolution . Creating Numerical Advantages And Controlling Possession The main purpose of inverting a full-back is to create an additional passing option in midfield. When Arsenal build from the back, one of their full-backs can move inside alongside the central midfielders, giving the team an extra player in the middle of the pitch. This makes it considerably more difficult for opponents to press Arsenal effectively. If an opposition midfielder follows the full-back into the centre, space can open up elsewhere. If they remain in position, Arsenal gain a numerical advantage. This is particularly important against opponents who defend with a compact shape. Rather than relying entirely on their centre-backs and midfielders to progress possession, Arsenal can create new passing angles and move the opposition’s defensive structure around. The result is a team that can patiently build attacks while maintaining control of central areas. (Photo by Clive Rose/Getty Images) Defensive Security And The Importance Of Player Profiles When Arsenal commit players forward, they inevitably leave spaces that opponents will look to exploit. Having a full-back positioned centrally can help reduce this risk. Instead of being caught too far up the pitch, the inverted full-back provides additional protection in front of the centre-backs, allowing Arsenal to maintain a stronger defensive structure when possession is lost. It also helps the team react quickly to transitions, attempting to win the ball back before the opposition can launch a dangerous counterattack. Of course, this approach is not without its risks. If opponents successfully bypass Arsenal’s initial pressure, the spaces left in wide areas can become vulnerable. Inverting also requires a different skill set from traditional wide defending. Players must be comfortable receiving the ball under pressure, making quick decisions and operating in congested midfield areas. They also need the positional awareness to understand when to move inside and when to provide width. item.description: Mandatory Credit: Robert Goddin-Imagn Images The Dallas Cowboys survived the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday in a game that was much closer than it should have been. Here’s what we learned. All but one punt came after the defense forced the Colts into three-and-outs. This was the second week in a row they held their opponent to just one score in the first half. Caleb Downs notched himself a sack on a blind side blitz while the defense never let Jonathan Taylor establish himself on the ground. item.title: Mohsin Naqvi's PCB backs Mike Hesson to continue as Pakistan's Test coach
item.description: Pakistan's white-ball head coach Mike Hesson will continue to look after the country's Test team as interim head coach until the end of the current World Test Championship (WTC) cycle. Hesson took charge of the red-ball side during Pakistan's difficult tour of England two months ago, after former coach Sarfaraz Ahmed was removed midway through the series. A source in the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) confirmed it to Indian news agency PTI that Hesson had agreed to continue in the role and would also guide the team during next year's Test series against New Zealand. "Hesson will also be interim head coach for next year's Test series against New Zealand. The board and head coach have both conveyed this to the players as well," the source said. Hesson's future with Pakistan cricket Hesson joined Pakistan as white-ball head coach in May 2025 before taking temporary charge of the Test team. However, his long-term future with the PCB will be reviewed after next year's World Cup, which will be jointly hosted by South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia. "Hesson's association with Pakistan cricket will be reviewed after next year's World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia. It will also then be decided who will be the head coach of the Test side for the next cycle of the World Test Championship," the source added. Questions over Hesson's influence Hesson has become a controversial figure in Pakistan cricket, with several former players and experts questioning the amount of authority he has been given by the PCB, particularly in team selection and other cricketing decisions. Pakistan Test captain Babar Azam also recently admitted that he does not have a say in selection matters. He said his responsibility is to make the best use of the 15-16 players selected by the team management and selection committee. The PCB source also acknowledged that chairman Mohsin Naqvi has great faith in Hesson and trusts him with important cricketing decisions. However, Hesson's frequent changes to the team and players across formats have not gone down well with everyone in Pakistan cricket.
